_about: The physics problem book's registry: key books and named classics. See principles/problem-books.md. Every named classic here is solved in a problem set; "where" points to it.
intro: Physics problems are worth doing when the answer surprises you. Each set asks for a guess first, then the calculation, then a check against a number you know.
lede: Pick a topic and guess before you calculate.

stage.title: By topic
stage.blurb: One set per area of physics, each running from warm-ups to hard problems, every one with a worked solution.

books.title: Problems in General Physics
books.author: I. E. Irodov
books.when: The classic: 1,900 short, sharp problems across all of first-year physics. Pick any chapter after the matching set here.

books.title: Physics Olympiad: Basic to Advanced Exercises
books.author: The Committee of Japan Physics Olympiad
books.when: Long problems that build an idea over several parts, with full solutions. For after P1–P3.

books.title: 200 Puzzling Physics Problems
books.author: Péter Gnädig, Gyula Honyek & Ken Riley
books.when: Clever problems that need one idea rather than a long calculation, with hints and solutions. Great for the guess-first habit.

books.title: Introduction to Classical Mechanics
books.author: David Morin
books.when: Hundreds of problems with full solutions, including a superb relativity section. Alongside P1 and P4.

books.title: An Introduction to Thermal Physics
books.author: Daniel V. Schroeder
books.when: Builds statistical mechanics from counting, with problems that compute real numbers. After P3.

books.title: Guesstimation
books.author: Lawrence Weinstein & John A. Adam
books.when: Order-of-magnitude estimates from everyday life. Any time, to sharpen the habit of checking an answer's size.

books.title: The Feynman Lectures on Physics
books.author: Richard Feynman, Robert Leighton & Matthew Sands
books.when: Not a problem book, but the best explanations to read when a solution here leaves you asking why. Free online at Caltech.

hard.title: The skier on the dome
hard.idea: A skier slides off a frictionless hemisphere. She leaves the surface when the normal force hits zero: at cos θ = 2/3, a third of the way down, whatever R, g or her mass.
hard.visual: The dome with the skier's path, the point of departure, and N(θ) falling to zero.

hard.title: The bead on a spinning hoop
hard.idea: Spin the hoop past √(g/R) and the bottom stops being stable; the bead picks a side. A pitchfork bifurcation, the simplest broken symmetry.
hard.visual: Equilibrium angle against spin rate: one branch splitting into two.

hard.title: The pendulum's real period
hard.idea: From horizontal, a pendulum takes 18% longer than Galileo's rule. The exact answer is an elliptic integral, or the arithmetic-geometric mean.
hard.visual: Two pendulums drifting apart, and T/T₀ against amplitude (interactive).

hard.title: The tennis racket theorem
hard.idea: Spin about the axis with the middle moment of inertia is unstable: Euler's equations give exponential growth of any wobble.
hard.visual: A spinning book flipping over, again and again.

hard.title: A tunnel through the Earth
hard.idea: Any straight frictionless tunnel takes 42 minutes end to end: Gauss's law makes the motion harmonic with the period of a grazing orbit.
hard.visual: Chords through a sphere, all crossed in the same time.

hard.title: The infinite resistor grid
hard.idea: Between adjacent nodes of an infinite square grid of resistors R, the resistance is exactly R/2: symmetry plus superposition.
hard.visual: Current spreading out from one node, and the superposed flow.

hard.title: The classical atom collapses
hard.idea: Larmor radiation makes a classical hydrogen atom spiral into its nucleus in 16 picoseconds. Atoms existing at all is evidence for quantum mechanics.
hard.visual: The shrinking spiral and its rising chirp.

hard.title: Gibbs's paradox
hard.idea: Mixing two identical gases can't raise the entropy, but classical counting says it does. Dividing by N! fixes it, for a reason only quantum mechanics explains.
hard.visual: A partition lifting between two gases, different and identical.

hard.title: The price of forgetting
hard.idea: A one-molecule engine extracts kT ln 2 from one bit of knowledge; erasing the bit costs at least as much. Maxwell's demon pays its bill.
hard.visual: The Szilard cycle: insert, measure, expand, erase.

hard.title: The twin paradox by birthday cards
hard.idea: Count the light signals each twin receives: 10 for one and 6 for the other, and both agree. The asymmetry is when each one sees the turnaround.
hard.visual: A spacetime diagram with the two streams of signals.

hard.title: Making the first antiproton
hard.idea: Making a proton–antiproton pair needs 6 m c² of beam energy on a fixed target, not 2: the invariant s explains why colliders collide.
hard.visual: Threshold energy against the mass made, fixed target vs collider.

hard.title: Three polarisers
hard.idea: Crossed polarisers block everything; add a third between them and a quarter gets through. Many small steps let almost everything through.
hard.visual: Transmitted fraction against the number of steps, approaching 1.
